This approach allows progressive force field building for complex systems like proteins, polymers, or mixed-material systems.

### Multi-Molecule Systems

Combine multiple AMBER-based molecules in a single system:

```python
# multi_molecule_system.lt
import "benzene.lt"
import "isobutane.lt"

write_once("Data Boundary") {
   0.0  60.00  xlo xhi
   0.0  60.00  ylo yhi
   0.0  60.00  zlo zhi
}

benzenes = new Benzene [32].move(6,0,0)
isobutanes = new Isobutane [32].move(0,6,0)
```

Moltemplate automatically merges force field parameters from all imported molecule definitions, handling type compatibility and parameter resolution.

Sources: [README.md](doc/doc_amber2lt.md#L38-L77), [README.md](examples/all_atom/force_field_AMBER/README.md#L15-L45)

- Explore [Force Field Parameter Management](15-force-field-parameter-management) for parameter optimization strategies
- Examine [mol22lt.py: MOL2 to LT Conversion](26-mol22lt-py-mol2-to-lt-conversion) for automated molecule generation
- Compare with [OPLSAA Force Field Integration](20-oplsaa-force-field-integration) for alternative all-atom approaches
- Review [Custom Force Field Development](23-custom-force-field-development) for advanced parameterization techniques

# DREIDING Force Field Integration



The DREIDING force field integration provides a comprehensive, all-atom force field implementation for molecular dynamics simulations in LAMMPS through moltemplate. Originally developed by Mayo et al. (1990), this implementation offers a generic force field designed for main-group elements including organic molecules, polymers, and inorganic materials. The integration provides automated parameter management, extensive atom type coverage, and seamless LAMMPS workflow integration.

## Architecture Overview

The DREIDING force field integration follows a systematic architecture that separates force field definitions from molecular system specification. The core force field is encapsulated in a single, comprehensive LT file (`moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt`) that contains all parameters and interaction rules, while system-specific files define molecular geometry and charge assignments.

![Furan Example](https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate/blob/master/examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/images/furan.jpg?raw=true) ![Right Arrow](https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate/blob/master/examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/images/rightarrow.svg?raw=true) ![Furan 5x5x10 t=0](https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate/blob/master/examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/images/furan_5x5x10_t=0.jpg?raw=true) ![Right Arrow](https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate/blob/master/examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/images/rightarrow.svg?raw=true) ![Furan 5x5x10 t=100ps](https://github.com/jewettaij/moltemplate/blob/master/examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/images/furan_5x5x10_t=100ps.jpg?raw=true)

Sources: [dreiding.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt#L1-L38315), [furan example](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/README.md#L1-L43)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[DREIDING Force Field] --> B[LAMMPS Initialization]
    A --> C[Atom Type Definitions]
    A --> D[Bonded Interactions]
    A --> E[Non-bonded Interactions]
    A --> F[Molecular Systems]
    
    B --> B1[units: real]
    B --> B2[atom_style: full]
    B --> B3[bond/angle_style: harmonic]
    B --> B4[dihedral_style: charmm]
    B --> B5[improper_style: umbrella]
    B --> B6[kspace_style: ewald]
    
    C --> C1[100+ Atom Types]
    C --> C2[Mass Definitions]
    C --> C3[Type-specific Coefficients]
    
    D --> D1[Bond Types]
    D --> D2[Angle Parameters]
    D --> D3[Dihedral Coefficients]
    D --> D4[Improper Parameters]
    
    E --> E1[LJ Pair Coefficients]
    E --> E2[Hydrogen Bonding]
    E --> E3[Coulombic Interactions]
    
    F --> F1[Molecule Definition]
    F --> F2[Charge Assignment]
    F --> F3[System Assembly]
```

## Force Field Implementation

### LAMMPS Configuration

The DREIDING force field requires specific LAMMPS settings configured through the `write_once("In Init")` block. These settings establish the fundamental simulation environment optimized for DREIDING's parameter set. The configuration uses real units (kcal/mol, Angstroms, fs) and harmonic potentials for bonds and angles. The force field employs CHARMM-style dihedrals with periodic boundaries and umbrella-style improper angles to maintain planarity and chirality. Long-range electrostatics are handled via Ewald summation with a tolerance of 0.0001.

Sources: [dreiding.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt#L17-L32)

| Setting | Value | Purpose |
|---------|-------|---------|
| units | real | kcal/mol, Å, fs units |
| atom_style | full | Molecular atoms with charge |
| bond_style | harmonic | Harmonic bond potential |
| angle_style | harmonic | Harmonic angle potential |
| dihedral_style | charmm | CHARMM periodic dihedrals |
| improper_style | umbrella | Umbrella improper potential |
| special_bonds | dreiding | 1-2, 1-3, 1-4 scaling factors |
| pair_style | hybrid/overlay hbond/dreiding/lj 4 6 6.5 90 lj/cut/coul/long 10.0 | LJ + hydrogen bonding |
| kspace_style | ewald 0.0001 | Long-range electrostatics |
| dielectric | 1.0 | Vacuum permittivity |

### Atom Type System

DREIDING employs a systematic atom type encoding scheme that captures element identity, hybridization, coordination, and hydrogen bonding capability. The naming convention follows the pattern `[Element]_[coordination][modifiers]`, where modifiers include resonance indicators (`R`), bond order specifications (`b1`, `b2`), and hydrogen bonding designators (`_hd` for donor, `_ha` for acceptor). This scheme enables precise specification of chemical environments across organic and inorganic molecules.

Sources: [dreiding.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt#L34-L122), [DREIDING_Label_Manual.pdf](doc/DREIDING_Label_Manual.pdf#L1-L200)

> [!TIP]
> The atom type encoding is systematic: element symbol + coordination number + optional modifiers. For example, `C_R_b1` indicates a carbon atom with resonance characteristics and a specific bond order variant, while `N_3_hd` represents a 3-coordinate nitrogen that can donate hydrogen bonds.

**Common Atom Type Examples:**

| Atom Type | Element | Coordination | Special Features |
|-----------|---------|--------------|------------------|
| H | Hydrogen | 1 | Standard hydrogen |
| H_HB | Hydrogen | 1 | Hydrogen bond participant |
| C_3 | Carbon | 3 | sp² hybridized |
| C_R | Carbon | Resonant | Aromatic/conjugated |
| C_2 | Carbon | 2 | sp hybridized |
| N_3 | Nitrogen | 3 | Standard 3-coordinate |
| N_R_d2 | Nitrogen | Resonant, double | Conjugated with double bond |
| O_R | Oxygen | Resonant | Aromatic/conjugated |
| O_3_hd | Oxygen | 3, H-bond donor | Can donate H-bonds |
| B_3 | Boron | 3 | Standard boron |

### Mass Definitions

The force field includes mass definitions for all 100+ atom types, with values drawn from standard atomic weights. These masses are automatically applied when atom types are assigned in molecular definitions. The mass table spans the periodic table from hydrogen (1.008 amu) through heavy elements like iodine (126.904 amu) and transition metals including iron (55.845 amu) and zinc (65.38 amu).

Sources: [dreiding.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt#L34-L122)

## Interaction Parameters

### Non-Bonded Interactions

Non-bonded interactions in DREIDING use a hybrid approach combining Lennard-Jones potentials with a specialized hydrogen bonding model. The pair style employs `hybrid/overlay` to simultaneously apply `lj/cut/coul/long` for van der Waals and Coulombic interactions and `hbond/dreiding/lj` for directional hydrogen bonding. This hybrid approach enables accurate modeling of both generic non-specific interactions and specific hydrogen bond geometries.

Sources: [dreiding.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt#L124-L699)

**Hydrogen Bonding Configuration:**
- H-bond cutoff: 4.0 Å
- Angle parameter: 2.75
- Well depth: 4.0 kcal/mol
- Exponent: 6
- Donor atom type: `*_hd`
- Acceptor atom type: `*_ha`

The Lennard-Jones parameters follow geometric combination rules derived from element-specific van der Waals radii. The force field includes explicit pair coefficients for all atom type combinations, covering interactions across the entire periodic table supported by DREIDING.

> [!TIP]
> DREIDING uses geometric combination rules for LJ parameters: ε<sub>ij</sub> = √(ε<sub>i</sub>ε<sub>j</sub>) and σ<sub>ij</sub> = (σ<sub>i</sub> + σ<sub>j</sub>)/2. All pair coefficients are explicitly defined in the force field file, eliminating the need for combination rules during simulation.

### Bonded Interactions

Bonded interactions include bonds, angles, dihedrals, and improper torsions, each defined with appropriate functional forms parameterized for the DREIDING force field. Bond types are defined systematically for all possible atom type combinations, enabling automatic bond coefficient assignment during system construction.

Sources: [dreiding.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt#L700-L1500)

**Bonded Interaction Summary:**

| Interaction | Style | Parameter Count | Coverage |
|-------------|-------|-----------------|----------|
| Bonds | Harmonic | 500+ types | All atom type combinations |
| Angles | Harmonic | Parameterized | Defined by central atom types |
| Dihedrals | CHARMM | Periodic | Based on atom type sequences |
| Impropers | Umbrella | Angle-dependent | Maintains planarity/chirality |

## Implementation Workflow

### Step 1: Import Force Field

Begin by importing the DREIDING force field definition in your LT file. The force field is automatically located by moltemplate if placed in the standard `force_fields` directory or available in the current working directory.

```lt
import "dreiding.lt"
```

Sources: [furan.lt](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/moltemplate_files/furan.lt#L1-L7)

### Step 2: Define Molecular Structure

Define your molecule by inheriting from the DREIDING base class and specifying atomic coordinates, types, and connectivity. Atom types must follow the DREIDING naming convention as documented in `DREIDING_Label_Manual.pdf`.

```lt
Furan inherits DREIDING {
  write("Data Atoms") {
    $atom:O0  $mol  @atom:O_R  -0.19    -0.790540 0.744310 -0.000000
    $atom:C0  $mol  @atom:C_R  -0.019   -1.909550 0.055400 0.000000
    $atom:C1  $mol  @atom:C_R  -0.019    0.227280 -0.086850 -0.000000
    # ... additional atoms
  }
  write("Data Bond List") {
    $bond:0	$atom:O0	$atom:C0
    $bond:1	$atom:O0	$atom:C1
    # ... additional bonds
  }
}
```

Sources: [furan.lt](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/moltemplate_files/furan.lt#L11-L44)

### Step 3: Assemble System

Create molecular arrays and define simulation boundaries. The example demonstrates creating a 5×5×10 lattice of furan molecules with appropriate periodic boundary conditions.

```lt
import "furan.lt"

molecule = new Furan [5].move(6.6,0,0)
                     [5].move(0,6.6,0)
                    [10].move(0,0,3.3)

write_once("Data Boundary") {
   0.0    33.0     xlo xhi
   0.0    33.0     ylo yhi
   0.0    33.0     zlo zhi
}
```

Sources: [system.lt](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/furan/moltemplate_files/system.lt#L1-L19)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Start] --> B[Import dreiding.lt]
    B --> C[Define Molecule<br/>assign atom types]
    C --> D[Define Connectivity<br/>bonds, angles, etc.]
    D --> E[Assign Partial Charges<br/>External tool required]
    E --> F[Assemble System<br/>molecular arrays]
    F --> G[Generate LAMMPS Files]
    G --> H[Run Simulation]
```

## Critical Implementation Considerations

### Partial Charge Assignment

**The most critical limitation of DREIDING in moltemplate is the lack of built-in partial charge assignment.** The DREIDING force field, as originally published, does not include rules or parameters for calculating atomic partial charges. Users must obtain charges through external methods.

**Recommended approaches:**

1. **QEq (Charge Equilibration)**: Use LAMMPS `fix qeq/point` to dynamically assign charges based on electronegativity equalization. This method is computationally efficient when run infrequently.

2. **Gasteiger Method**: An empirical approach suggested in the original DREIDING paper that estimates charges based on atomic connectivity and electronegativity differences.

3. **Quantum Chemistry Calculations**: Perform DFT or semi-empirical calculations to obtain electrostatic potential (ESP) charges.

4. **Charges from Other Force Fields**: **NOT RECOMMENDED** - Using charges from OPLSAA or AMBER parameters (as shown in the examples) may produce unphysical results because charge sets are force field-specific.

Sources: [README.md](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/README.md#L17-L31)

> [!TIP]
> The example charges in the repository are intentionally incorrect as they were borrowed from OPLSAA parameters for demonstration purposes only. Do not use these charges for production simulations. Implement a proper charge calculation workflow using QEq, Gasteiger, or quantum chemistry methods.

### Improper Angle Symmetry

Improper angles in DREIDING depend on atom ordering around a central atom. When multiple atoms have identical types, moltemplate cannot guarantee consistent ordering, which may lead to different improper angle assignments across identical molecules. This ambiguity stems from the force field's reliance on specific atom sequences rather than purely topological definitions.

Sources: [README.md](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/README.md#L25-L31)

### Experimental Status

The DREIDING force field integration in moltemplate is **experimental and not fully validated**. Testing has been limited to simple molecules (butane and ethylene) for consistency with Materials Studio. Users should verify their simulation results against independent calculations or experimental data and report any bugs encountered.

Sources: [README.md](examples/all_atom/force_field_DREIDING/README.md#L4-L11)


## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Incorrect physical behavior | Wrong partial charges | Use QEq or proper quantum chemistry calculations |
| Missing atom types | Non-DREIDING elements | Extend force field or use different force field |
| Improper angle errors | Symmetric atom ordering | Manually verify improper definitions |
| Large output files | All parameters included | Use cleanup scripts to remove unused types |
| Simulation crashes | Missing pair coefficients | Verify all atom type combinations have defined LJ parameters |

## Advanced Usage and Customization

For researchers requiring modifications to the DREIDING force field, the modular structure enables custom parameter additions. Atom types, pair coefficients, and bonded parameters can be extended by adding entries following the existing naming conventions and parameter formats. Users should refer to the original DREIDING publication (Mayo et al., J. Phys. Chem. 1990, 94, 8897-8909) for parameter calculation methodologies.

Sources: [dreiding.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/dreiding.lt#L1-L38315)

# Custom Force Field Development



Custom force field development in moltemplate enables researchers to create, modify, and extend molecular mechanics force fields for specialized simulation needs. This capability bridges the gap between published force field parameters and LAMMPS implementation, providing both manual construction and automated conversion pathways. Understanding the force field architecture and available conversion tools empowers developers to work with specialized chemical systems that fall outside standard force field coverage.

## Force Field Architecture Overview

A moltemplate force field file follows a structured object-oriented design pattern where all parameters are encapsulated within a single object that can be inherited by molecular definitions. This architecture separates concerns between parameter definition and molecular instantiation, promoting code reuse and maintainability across complex simulation systems.

```mermaid
graph TB
    A["Force Field Object"] --> B["Atom Definitions"]
    A --> C["Equivalence Categories"]
    A --> D["Non-bonded Parameters"]
    A --> E["Bonded Parameters"]
    A --> F["Interaction Type Rules"]
    
    B --> B1["Atomic Charges"]
    B --> B2["Atomic Masses"]
    
    C --> C1["Bond Types"]
    C --> C2["Angle Types"]
    C --> C3["Dihedral Types"]
    C --> C4["Improper Types"]
    
    D --> D1["LJ σ/ε"]
    D --> D2["Coulombic"]
    
    E --> E1["Bond Coefficients"]
    E --> E2["Angle Coefficients"]
    E --> E3["Dihedral Coefficients"]
    E --> E4["Improper Coefficients"]
    
    F --> F1["Bonds By Type"]
    F --> F2["Angles By Type"]
    F --> F3["Dihedrals By Type"]
    F --> F4["Impropers By Type"]
    
    style A fill:#e1f5fe
    style B fill:#fff9c4
    style C fill:#fff9c4
    style D fill:#c8e6c9
    style E fill:#c8e6c9
    style F fill:#f8bbd9
```

The force field object serves as a parameter repository that defines all atom types, interaction coefficients, and mapping rules. When a molecule inherits from this object, it gains access to these parameters without needing to redefine them. The `oplsaa_simple.lt` file provides a pedagogical example demonstrating this structure with minimal atom types for simple alkanes and alkenes.
Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L1-L50)

## Atom Type Definition and Assignment

Atom types form the foundation of any force field, determining both non-bonded interactions and bonded interaction parameters. In moltemplate, atom types use the `@atom:` namespace prefix and can optionally include multiple identifiers for different interaction categories using the equivalence category system.

**Charge Assignment Methods**: Moltemplate supports two primary approaches for assigning partial charges: type-based assignment and bond-increment assignment. Type-based assignment uses the LAMMPS `set type` command to assign fixed charges to all atoms of a given type, while bond-increment assignment allows charge values to depend on the chemical environment through additive contributions from bonded neighbors.
Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L31-L42)

```lt
write_once("In Charges") {
    set type @atom:CT3H        charge -0.18
    set type @atom:CT2H        charge -0.12
    set type @atom:HCan        charge  0.06
}
```

For bond-increment charges, you define pairs of atom types with incremental charge contributions that are summed for each atom based on its bonded neighbors:

```lt
write_once("Data Charge By Bond") {
    @atom:C_sp3 @atom:H 0.05 -0.05
}
```

**Equivalence Categories**: One of moltemplate's most powerful features is the ability to assign separate type identifiers for different interaction types within a single atom type. This enables fine-grained control over interaction parameters while maintaining a single user-facing atom type. The `replace` command establishes these mappings: Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L68-L75)

```lt
replace{ @atom:CT3H @atom:CT3H_bCT_aCT_dCT_iCT }
```

In this example, `bCT` identifies the atom for bond parameter lookup, `aCT` for angles, `dCT` for dihedrals, and `iCT` for impropers. This separation allows the same atom type to participate in different interaction classes with appropriate parameters.

## Non-Bonded Interaction Parameters

Non-bonded interactions define van der Waals and electrostatic forces between atoms. These are specified using `pair_coeff` directives within the `write_once("In Settings")` block. The syntax follows LAMMPS conventions where the first two arguments specify atom types and remaining arguments depend on the pair style being used.
Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L85-L94)

```lt
write_once("In Settings") {
    pair_coeff @atom:CT3H_bCT_aCT_dCT_iCT  @atom:CT3H_bCT_aCT_dCT_iCT  0.066 3.5
    pair_coeff @atom:HCan_bHC_aHC_dHC_iHC  @atom:HCan_bHC_aHC_dHC_iHC  0.03 2.5
}
```

For cross-interactions between different atom types, you can either specify explicit coefficients or rely on mixing rules. When using mixing rules, you only need to define same-type coefficients, and LAMMPS automatically computes cross-interaction parameters.

> [!TIP]
> **Critical Parameter Selection**: When developing custom force fields, ensure that your σ (sigma) and ε (epsilon) parameters are consistent with the Lennard-Jones potential form used by your LAMMPS pair style. Different pair styles (lj/cut, lj/charmm, lj/cut/coul/long, etc.) may interpret these parameters differently, particularly regarding the energy and length unit conventions.

## Bonded Interaction Parameters

Bonded interactions include bonds (2-body), angles (3-body), dihedrals (4-body), and impropers (4-body). Each interaction type requires coefficient definitions and type assignment rules.

**Bond Coefficients**: Bonds use harmonic potentials by default, requiring force constant and equilibrium bond length parameters: Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L101-L110)

```lt
write_once("In Settings") {
    bond_coeff @bond:CT_CT   268.0 1.529
    bond_coeff @bond:CT_HC  340.0 1.09
}
```

**Angle Coefficients**: Angles define three-atom interactions and are specified similarly with force constant and equilibrium angle: Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L125-L138)

```lt
write_once("In Settings") {
    angle_coeff @angle:CT_CT_CT   58.35 112.7
    angle_coeff @angle:HC_CT_HC  33.0 107.8
}
```

**Dihedral Coefficients**: Dihedrals define four-atom torsional interactions. Multiple functional forms exist (OPLS, CHARMM, harmonic), with the OPLS style being common for all-atom force fields: Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L147-L172)

```lt
write_once("In Settings") {
    dihedral_coeff @dihedral:X_CT_CT_CT  1.711 -0.5 0.663 0.0
    dihedral_coeff @dihedral:CT_CT_CT_CT  1.3 -0.05 0.2 0.0
}
```

The OPLS dihedral style uses Fourier series coefficients (K₁, K₂, K₃, K₄) representing different periodicity terms. General dihedral types with wildcards allow fallback behavior, while specific types override general rules.

## Automated Interaction Type Assignment

Instead of manually specifying bond, angle, dihedral, and improper types for each interaction in your molecular definitions, moltemplate can automatically generate these interactions based on atom type patterns using the "By Type" sections. This dramatically reduces the complexity of molecular definition files and ensures consistency.
Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L113-L119)

**Bond Type Assignment Rules**: The `Data Bonds By Type` section defines mapping rules from atom types to bond types:

```lt
write_once("Data Bonds By Type") {
    @bond:CT_CT @atom:*_bCT_a*_d*_i* @atom:*_bCT_a*_d*_i*
    @bond:CT_HC @atom:*_bCT_a*_d*_i* @atom:*_bHC_a*_d*_i*
}
```

The wildcard character `*` matches any value in that position. This rule states that whenever two atoms both have bond type identifiers ending in `_bCT`, create a bond interaction of type `@bond:CT_CT` between them.

**Angle Type Assignment Rules**: Angles follow a similar pattern but involve three atoms:

```lt
write_once("Data Angles By Type") {
    @angle:CT_CT_CT @atom:*_b*_aCT_d*_i* @atom:*_b*_aCT_d*_i* @atom:*_b*_aCT_d*_i*
}
```

Here, the middle atom's angle type identifier (`aCT`) is used for matching, while bond and dihedral identifiers can be anything.

**Dihedral Type Assignment Rules**: Dihedrals involve four atoms with more complex matching patterns:

```lt
write_once("Data Dihedrals By Type") {
    @dihedral:X_CT_CT_CT @atom:*_b*_a*_dCT_i* @atom:*_b*_a*_dCT_i* @atom:*_b*_a*_dCT_i* @atom:*_b*_a*_dCT_i*
}
```

The central bond's dihedral type identifier (`dCT`) determines the dihedral type. Wildcards allow general rules that match many different atom combinations.

The `nbody_by_type.py` utility processes these rules during moltemplate execution, automatically generating the appropriate bond, angle, dihedral, and improper interactions based on the actual connectivity in your molecular system. This enables the "write once, apply everywhere" paradigm where force field rules are defined once and automatically applied to all molecules that use the force field.
Sources: [nbody_by_type.py](moltemplate/nbody_by_type.py#L1-L100)

## Force Field Conversion Tools

Moltemplate provides several conversion utilities that automate the process of creating custom force fields from existing parameter files in various formats. These tools handle the complex task of parsing proprietary formats and generating properly structured moltemplate files.

### OPLSAA Force Field Conversion

The `oplsaa2lt.py` script converts BOSS input files (`.par` and `.sb`) into moltemplate format. BOSS (Biochemical and Organic Simulation System) is a popular molecular simulation package that distributes OPLS-AA parameters in a specialized format.
Sources: [oplsaa2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L1-L50)

```bash
./oplsaa2lt.py --name OPLSAA --out oplsaa2024.lt \
  --par oplsaa.par \
  --sb  oplsaa.sb
```

The conversion process handles atom type renaming to avoid conflicts with moltemplate syntax (characters like `:`, `$`, `#`, `*` are replaced with safer alternatives). The script creates a comprehensive force field object with all atom types, masses, charges, pair coefficients, bonded parameters, and interaction type rules.
Sources: [oplsaa2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L30-L50)

**Type Name Cleaning**: The conversion includes automatic sanitization of atom type names:

```python
TYPE_CONVERSION_TUPLES = (
    ('C:', "C°"),
    ("C$", "C^"),
    ("N$", "N^"),
    ("O$", "O^"),
    ("C#", "C|"),
    ("N*", "N§"),
    ("C(O)", "C⟮"),
)
```

This ensures compatibility with moltemplate's parser while preserving the semantic meaning of the original type names.

### TINKER Parameter File Conversion

The `tinkerparm2lt.py` script converts TINKER parameter files (`.prm`) into moltemplate format. TINKER is another molecular modeling package that distributes several force fields including OPLS-AA variants.
Sources: [tinkerparm2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py#L1-L50)

```bash
tinkerparm2lt.py -name OPLS < oplsaa.prm > oplsaa2008.lt
```

This script has been tested primarily with OPLS-AA force fields but may work with other TINKER-compatible force fields. Note that some force fields requiring advanced features like point-dipole polarizability may not be fully convertible due to LAMMPS feature limitations as of 2017.
Sources: [tinkerparm2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py#L12-L25)

### AMBER Force Field Conversion

The `amber2lt.py` script converts AMBER FRCMOD and DAT files into moltemplate format. This is particularly useful for working with GAFF (General AMBER Force Field) and custom AMBER-style force fields.
Sources: [doc_amber2lt.md](doc/doc_amber2lt.md#L1-L50)

```bash
amber2lt.py --in gaff.dat --name GAFF --out gaff.lt
```

The generated force field file includes all standard AMBER atom types and parameters. Combined with `mol22lt.py` for MOL2 file conversion, this provides a complete workflow for AMBER-based simulations in LAMMPS: Sources: [gaff.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/gaff.lt#L1-L50)

```bash
amber2lt.py --in benzene.frcmod --name MyForceField >> my_force_field.lt
mol22lt.py --in benzene.mol2 --out benzene.lt --name Benzene \
           --ff MyForceField --ff-file my_force_field.lt
```

### MOL2 File Conversion

The `mol22lt.py` script converts MOL2 molecular structure files into moltemplate molecule definitions. This tool extracts atomic charges, coordinates, atom types, and connectivity from MOL2 files and generates properly formatted molecule objects.
Sources: [doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L1-L50)

```bash
mol22lt.py \
   --in PPS_5mer.mol2 \
   --out PPS_5mer.lt \
   --name PPS5 \
   --ff GAFF2 \
   --ff-file "gaff2.lt"
```

**Important Limitations**: The current version (beta as of 2024-12-05) does not support MOL2 files with multiple chains. The script extracts charge, atom names, coordinates, atom types, subunit information, and bonds from the ATOM and BOND sections, ignoring chain information and other metadata.
Sources: [doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L54-L100)

## Building Custom Molecules with Force Fields

Once a force field is defined or converted, you can create molecular definitions that inherit from it. The `ch3.lt` and `ch2.lt` files in the usage examples demonstrate this pattern for simple alkane building blocks.
Sources: [ch3.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/usage_example/ch3.lt#L1-L40)

```lt
import "oplsaa_simple.lt"

CH3 inherits OPLSAA {
  write("Data Atoms") {
    $atom:C  $mol:... @atom:CT3H   0.0  0.000000     0.000000      0.000000
    $atom:H1 $mol:... @atom:HCan  0.0  0.000000     0.631044      0.892431
    $atom:H2 $mol:... @atom:HCan  0.0  0.000000     0.631044     -0.892431
    $atom:H3 $mol:... @atom:HCan  0.0 -0.892431    -0.631044      0.000000
  }
  write('Data Bond List') {
    $bond:CH1 $atom:C $atom:H1
    $bond:CH2 $atom:C $atom:H2
    $bond:CH3 $atom:C $atom:H3
  }
}
```

Note that atomic charges can be set to 0.0 in the molecule definition if the force field uses type-based charge assignment. The `$mol:...` syntax indicates that this molecule may be part of a larger molecular structure and should use the parent object's molecule ID.
Sources: [ch3.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/usage_example/ch3.lt#L15-L33)

**Polymer Construction**: The `alkane50.lt` example demonstrates building long-chain polymers by combining smaller monomer units. This approach enables efficient construction of large molecules with consistent parameters: Sources: [alkane50.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/usage_example/alkane50.lt#L1-L50)

```lt
import "ch2.lt"
import "ch3.lt"

Alkane50 inherits OPLSAA {
  create_var {$mol}
  
  monomers = new CH2 [50].rot(180,1,0,0).move(1.2533223,0,0)
  
  delete monomers[0]
  delete monomers[49]
  monomers[0] = new CH3
  monomers[49] = new CH3.rot(180.0,0,0,1).move(61.4127927,0,0)
}
```

The array creation syntax with transformations allows rapid construction of repetitive structures while the bond list section defines inter-monomer connectivity. Angles, dihedrals, and impropers are automatically generated by the type assignment rules defined in the force field.
Sources: [alkane50.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/usage_example/alkane50.lt#L55-L95)

> [!TIP]
> **Validation Strategy**: When developing custom force fields, validate each component incrementally. Start with a small test molecule containing all relevant atom types. Verify that charges are correctly assigned, then check non-bonded interactions through a simple energy minimization. Finally, validate bonded interactions by comparing structural properties (bond lengths, angles, dihedral distributions) against experimental or quantum chemical data.

## Best Practices for Force Field Development

**Modular Design**: Organize your force field into logical sections with clear comments documenting the source and validity of parameters. Include citations for published parameters and notes for any custom modifications. The `oplsaa.lt` file demonstrates good documentation practice with header comments indicating generation method and parameter sources.
Sources: [oplsaa.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/oplsaa.lt#L1-L30)

**Naming Conventions**: Establish consistent naming conventions for atom types and interaction types. Use descriptive names that reflect chemical environment (e.g., `CT3H` for CH₃ carbon with three hydrogens). The OPLS-AA force field uses systematic two-letter type identifiers that encode hybridization and connectivity information.
Sources: [oplsaa.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/oplsaa.lt#L31-L60)

**Testing Incrementally**: Build and test your force field progressively. Start with a minimal subset of atom types and parameters, validate against reference data, then expand systematically. The `build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt` example provides a template for this approach, containing only the minimal types needed for simple alkanes.
Sources: [oplsaa_simple.lt](moltemplate/force_fields/build_your_own_force_field/oplsaa_simple.lt#L1-L20)

**Leverage Conversion Tools**: When working with existing force fields, prefer conversion tools over manual parameter entry to avoid transcription errors. The `oplsaa2lt.py`, `tinkerparm2lt.py`, and `amber2lt.py` scripts have been tested with standard parameter files and handle edge cases properly.
Sources: [convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md#L1-L30)

## Integration with LAMMPS Simulation Pipeline

Once your custom force field and molecular definitions are complete, moltemplate generates the necessary LAMMPS input files through the standard moltemplate.sh workflow. The force field parameters appear in the generated data file's appropriate sections and the input script contains necessary pair_style, bond_style, and other style specifications.

The generated force field includes all `write_once("In Settings")` directives, which are emitted exactly once to the LAMMPS input script regardless of how many molecules inherit from the force field. This prevents parameter duplication and ensures consistent application across the entire system.

For complex force fields requiring specialized LAMMPS features (e.g., tabulated potentials, many-body interactions, polarizable force fields), you may need to add custom `write_once("In Settings")` blocks with the appropriate LAMMPS commands. Moltemplate's flexibility allows integration of any LAMMPS-supported interaction style through these custom blocks.

## Next Steps

After creating your custom force field, you can:

- **Expand to complex systems**: Combine multiple custom force fields using LAMMPS hybrid pair styles for multi-component simulations
- **Validate performance**: Benchmark your force field against experimental data or higher-level calculations using the examples in [examples/all_atom/](examples/all_atom/) and [examples/coarse_grained/](examples/coarse_grained/)
- **Optimize parameters**: Use LAMMPS simulation tools for parameter refinement through iterative testing and validation
- **Distribute your force field**: Share your custom force field as an `.lt` file with the community, following the pattern of existing force fields in [moltemplate/force_fields/](moltemplate/force_fields/)

For deeper understanding of the template system that powers force field inheritance and parameter application, explore [Core Template System Architecture](7-core-template-system-architecture). To understand how bonded interactions are automatically generated from type assignment rules, see [Bond Detection by Atom Type](16-bond-detection-by-atom-type) and [Angle, Dihedral, and Improper Generation](17-angle-dihedral-and-improper-generation).

# Force Field Conversion Tools



Moltemplate provides a comprehensive suite of conversion tools that translate force field parameters from multiple molecular simulation packages into moltemplate's LT (LAMMPS Template) format. These tools enable researchers to leverage existing force field libraries—including AMBER, OPLS-AA, COMPASS, TINKER, and EMC formats—within moltemplate's template-based simulation framework. The conversion architecture handles bonded parameters, non-bonded interactions, equivalences, and wildcard patterns while preserving the hierarchical parameter selection rules that characterize each force field's design philosophy.

## Conversion Architecture Overview

The force field conversion infrastructure is organized around format-specific converters located in `moltemplate/force_fields/convert_*` directories. Each converter implements a three-stage pipeline: parsing force-field specific input files, transforming parameter definitions into moltemplate syntax, and generating structured LT files that can be imported directly into moltemplate simulations. The conversion process automatically handles complex aspects such as wildcard atom types ("X" or "*"), parameter equivalences across atom types, duplicate parameter resolution, and unit conversions where required.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph InputFormats["Force Field Formats"]
        AMBER["AMBER<br/>(.frcmod, .dat)"]
        OPLSAA["OPLS-AA<br/>(.par, .sb)"]
        MSI["MSI/BIOSYM<br/>(.frc)"]
        TINKER["TINKER<br/>(.prm)"]
        EMC["EMC<br/>(.prm)"]
        MOL2["MOL2<br/>(.mol2)"]
    end

    subgraph Converters["Conversion Tools"]
        A2LT["amber2lt.py"]
        O2LT["oplsaa2lt.py"]
        M2LT["msifrc2lt.py"]
        T2LT["tinkerparm2lt.py"]
        E2LT["emcprm2lt.py"]
        M22LT["mol22lt.py"]
    end

    subgraph Output["Moltemplate LT Files"]
        LT["Force Field Objects<br/>Atom Types<br/>Bond/Angle/Dihedral Rules<br/>Non-Bonded Parameters"]
    end

    AMBER --> A2LT
    OPLSAA --> O2LT
    MSI --> M2LT
    TINKER --> T2LT
    EMC --> E2LT
    MOL2 --> M22LT
    
    A2LT --> LT
    O2LT --> LT
    M2LT --> LT
    T2LT --> LT
    E2LT --> LT
    M22LT --> LT
```

The converters share common architectural patterns while handling format-specific nuances. Each converter reads parameter tables, processes wildcard and equivalence rules, sorts interaction definitions to ensure proper priority (generic before specific), and outputs moltemplate-compatible syntax using the `write_once()` and `write()` directives. The resulting LT files define force field objects that can be inherited by molecule definitions, enabling consistent parameter application across simulation systems.

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/README.txt](moltemplate/force_fields/README.txt#L1-L14), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py](moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L7-L11), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md#L1-L18)

## AMBER Force Field Conversion

The `amber2lt.py` converter transforms AMBER force field files (FRCMOD and DAT formats) into moltemplate LT format. AMBER force fields utilize wildcard atom types ("X") to define generic parameters that apply when specific parameters are not available—a pattern that requires careful handling during conversion to maintain the hierarchical parameter lookup strategy.

The conversion process extracts parameter sections for masses, bonds, angles, dihedrals, impropers, and pair (non-bonded) interactions. A critical sorting operation ensures wildcard-containing interactions appear before specific interactions in the output LT file, as moltemplate processes "By Type" rules sequentially and gives priority to the last matching rule [moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L189-L200]. This inversion of the AMBER convention (where specific rules are searched first) enables moltemplate's pattern matching to correctly select the most specific parameter.

The converter transforms AMBER atom type naming by replacing "*" with "star" to avoid moltemplate syntax conflicts while preserving the wildcard functionality through pattern matching [moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L234-L290]. Bond parameters are converted to harmonic style, angles to harmonic style, dihedrals to Fourier series representation, and pair interactions to Lennard-Jones with Coulombic long-range corrections.

**Command-line interface example:**
```bash
moltemplate/amber2lt.py --in gaff.dat --out gaff.lt --name GAFF
```

**Python API usage:**
```python
from moltemplate.amber2lt import ConvertAmber2Lt
with open('gaff.dat', 'r') as f:
    lines = f.readlines()
lt_content = ConvertAmber2Lt('GAFF', lines)
```

The conversion supports optional separation of parameter types via command-line arguments (`--mass`, `--bond`, `--angle`, etc.) when force field parameters are distributed across multiple files. The resulting LT file defines a force field object containing atom type definitions with comments, mass tables, and interaction rules organized by moltemplate's data structure conventions.

Sources: [doc/doc_amber2lt.md](doc/doc_amber2lt.md#L10-L20), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py](moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L7-L11), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py](moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L189-L200), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py](moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L234-L290), [moltemplate/amber2lt.py](moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L767-L800)

## MOL2 to Moltemplate Conversion

The `mol22lt.py` converter serves a distinct purpose from the other force field converters: it translates MOL2 molecular structure files into moltemplate format, creating molecule definitions with explicit coordinates and bond connectivity. This tool is designed for importing pre-parametrized molecules from external databases or quantum chemistry packages, allowing researchers to quickly integrate experimentally or computationally derived structures into moltemplate workflows.

The MOL2 converter extracts atom information (IDs, names, coordinates, types, charges), bond definitions, and molecular subunits from the TRIPOS-formatted MOL2 file [moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L76-L140]. When converting multi-chain systems or multiple molecules in a single file, the tool can merge molecule IDs when a single object name is specified via the `--name` argument, or preserve separate subunit definitions for independent manipulation.

**Key features include:**
- External charge file support via `--charges` argument
- Atom type capitalization control (`--upper-case-types`, `--lower-case-types`)
- Atom name capitalization control (`--upper-case-names`, `--lower-case-names`)
- Optional force field association via `--ff` and `--ff-file` arguments
- Bond type inclusion option for parameterized bond definitions

**Command-line usage:**
```bash
moltemplate/mol22lt.py --in molecule.mol2 --out molecule.lt --name MOLECULE
```

The converter generates LT files with structured molecule definitions including atom coordinate tables (`write('Data Atoms')`), bond lists (`write('Data Bond List')` or `write('Data Bonds')` depending on parameter availability), and usage instructions. Importantly, mol22lt does **not** automatically assign force field parameters—it relies on external force field files (such as those generated by amber2lt.py or oplsaa2lt.py) to provide interaction parameters. The tool focuses on structural representation, leaving parameter assignment to the force field inheritance mechanism.

A significant limitation is the current handling of multiple chains in a single file. The tool can either merge all chains into a single molecule object or preserve them as separate subunits, but complex chain connectivity and hierarchical relationships may require manual post-processing [doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L60-L102].

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L10-L22), [doc/doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L60-L102), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L76-L140), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L400-L480)

## OPLS-AA Force Field Conversion

The OPLS-AA converter (`oplsaa2lt.py`) handles the unique two-file format used by BOSS (Biochemical and Organic Simulation System): a `.par` file containing atom type definitions and torsion/improper parameters, and a `.sb` file containing bond and angle parameters [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L320-L380]. This separation reflects the modular structure of OPLS-AA force fields, which have evolved through multiple versions (OPLS-AA 2008, OPLS-AA 2024) with increasing parameter coverage.

The conversion process involves parsing both files, extracting interaction definitions, then performing duplicate removal and sorting operations. OPLS-AA files contain extensive redundant parameter definitions for the same atom type combinations, requiring sophisticated duplicate resolution logic [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L171-L275]. The converter implements William Jorgensen's recommended strategy: when duplicate interactions exist for identical atom types, the most general interaction (as indicated by duplicate count and position in the original PAR file) should be sorted to appear last in the LT file, allowing moltemplate to select it only when more specific parameters don't match.

The converter also handles OPLS-AA's distinctive type naming conventions, which use numeric codes (e.g., "143" for alkene carbon) rather than descriptive names. A type conversion system maintains cross-references between numeric codes and chemical descriptions [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L26-L37], preserving documentation while generating numeric type identifiers suitable for moltemplate.

**Command-line usage:**
```bash
./oplsaa2lt.py --name OPLSAA --out oplsaa2024.lt \
  --par oplsaa.par \
  --sb  oplsaa.sb
```

The resulting LT file defines an OPLSAA force field object with complete parameter tables, suitable for use in molecule definitions through inheritance:

```lt
import "oplsaa2024.lt"

Ethylene inherits OPLSAA {
  write('Data Atoms') {
    $atom:c1  $mol @atom:143  0.00 -0.6695   0.00000  0.000
    $atom:h11 $mol @atom:144  0.00 -1.23422 -0.85446  0.000
  }
  write('Data Bond List') {
    $bond:c1h1 $atom:c1 $atom:h11
  }
}
```

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/README.md#L1-L54), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L320-L380), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L171-L275)

## MSI/BIOSYM Force Field Conversion

The `msifrc2lt.py` converter processes MSI-format force field files (also known as BIOSYM, Accelrys, or DISCOVERY formats), which are historically significant in molecular simulation but use complex parameter matching strategies. These files define atom type equivalences and "auto-equivalences" that enable sophisticated wildcard pattern matching beyond the simple "X" wildcard used in AMBER.

The conversion architecture implements a multi-stage equivalence processing system [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_MSI_files_to_LT_files/msifrc2lt.py#L662-L720]. For each atom type, the converter generates a comprehensive force field identifier string (ffid) that concatenates the original atom type with equivalence markers for pair interactions, bonds, angles, dihedrals, and impropers. When moltemplate searches for interaction parameters, it pattern-matches against these extended strings, enabling the complex inheritance hierarchies that characterize MSI force fields.

The converter handles several MSI-specific features:
- Priority-based atom matching where wildcard atoms are followed by integer priority numbers
- Auto-equivalence systems that determine atom type compatibility based on local chemical context
- Version-based parameter prioritization when multiple parameter sets exist
- Out-of-plane (OOP) and Class-2 improper style definitions with distinct atom ordering conventions

A significant limitation is the current disregard of "template" information contained in MSI files. These templates typically define rules for automatic atom type assignment based on local bonding patterns, but msifrc2lt.py requires users to manually select appropriate atom types when defining molecules [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_MSI_files_to_LT_files/msifrc2lt.py#L6-L32]. This limitation means the converter is best suited for force field translation rather than automated molecule parameterization.

> [!TIP]
> The MSI converter's equivalence system is powerful but complex. When debugging parameter assignment issues, examine the generated "force field identifier" strings in the LT file—they contain the concatenation of atom types with ~p, ~b, ~a, ~d, and ~i suffixes representing pair, bond, angle, dihedral, and improper equivalences respectively.

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_MSI_files_to_LT_files/msifrc2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_MSI_files_to_LT_files/msifrc2lt.py#L6-L32), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_MSI_files_to_LT_files/msifrc2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_MSI_files_to_LT_files/msifrc2lt.py#L662-L720)

## TINKER and EMC Force Field Conversion

The TINKER (`tinkerparm2lt.py`) and EMC (`emcprm2lt.py`) converters provide access to additional force field ecosystems. The TINKER converter handles `.prm` files containing the complete force field parameterization, with specific support for the OPLS-AA parameter set distributed with TINKER [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py#L9-L21]. The converter supports multiple interaction styles through command-line flags, enabling adaptation to various LAMMPS pair, bond, angle, dihedral, and improper styles.

**TINKER converter features:**
- Atom type subset selection via `-atoms` argument
- Customizable LAMMPS interaction styles (`-dihedral-style`, `-pair-style`, etc.)
- Support for both local files and URL-based parameter files
- Zero-padding options for force field IDs
- Hybrid/overlay style selection for complex potential functions

**TINKER command-line usage:**
```bash
./tinkerparm2lt.py -file oplsaa.prm -name OPLSAA -dihedral-style opls
```

The EMC converter specializes in EMC-format parameter files, which are characterized by explicit unit definitions and modular organization of potential functions [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_EMC_files_to_LT_files/emcprm2lt.py#L22-L80]. The converter automatically detects units (length, energy, density) and performs conversions to LAMMPS "real" units when necessary. It includes customizable potential style support and generates initialization scripts (`write_once("In Init")`) with appropriate LAMMPS commands for the selected potential functions.

**EMC converter features:**
- Automatic unit conversion from non-LAMMPS units
- Customizable potential styles for all interaction types
- Support for multi-file input (concatenated parameter files)
- Generic initialization script generation
- Special bonds handling for 1-4 interactions

**EMC command-line usage:**
```bash
./emcprm2lt.py file1.prm file2.prm --bond-style=harmonic --angle-style=harmonic --name=FF_NAME
```

Both converters include warning systems for untested parameter combinations and recommend manual verification of generated LT files, particularly for complex potential styles or unusual unit systems.

Sources: [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py#L9-L21), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_TINKER_files_to_LT_files/tinkerparm2lt.py#L117-L250), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_EMC_files_to_LT_files/emcprm2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_EMC_files_to_LT_files/emcprm2lt.py#L22-L80)

## Conversion Tool Comparison and Selection

The force field conversion tools exhibit both shared patterns and format-specific specializations. Understanding these characteristics helps researchers select the appropriate tool for their workflow and interpret the resulting LT files correctly.

| **Converter** | **Input Format** | **Output Focus** | **Wildcards** | **Equivalences** | **Unit Conversion** |
|---------------|-----------------|------------------|---------------|------------------|---------------------|
| `amber2lt.py` | FRCMOD/DAT | Force field parameters | Simple ("X") | Basic | No |
| `mol22lt.py` | MOL2 | Molecule structure | N/A | N/A | N/A |
| `oplsaa2lt.py` | .par + .sb | Force field parameters | None | Duplicate handling | No |
| `msifrc2lt.py` | .FRC | Force field parameters | Complex (priority) | Advanced | No |
| `tinkerparm2lt.py` | .prm | Force field parameters | None | Basic | No |
| `emcprm2lt.py` | .prm | Force field parameters | None | Basic | Yes |

> [!TIP]
> When troubleshooting parameter assignment issues, remember that moltemplate processes "By Type" interaction rules in the order they appear in the LT file, applying the **last** matching rule. Converters that use wildcards deliberately sort generic rules before specific rules to ensure specific parameters override generic ones—the reverse of how some source formats organize their parameter tables.

**Selection guidelines:**

- **Use `amber2lt.py`** when working with AMBER force fields (GAFF, GAFF2, AMBER biomolecular force fields) that use the standard AMBER parameter format with wildcard support.

- **Use `mol22lt.py`** when you have MOL2 files from databases (PubChem, ZINC) or quantum chemistry packages and need to create molecule definitions with explicit coordinates. Remember to pair with an appropriate force field file.

- **Use `oplsaa2lt.py`** for the latest OPLS-AA force fields (particularly the 2024 update) which are distributed as BOSS .par and .sb file pairs.

- **Use `msifrc2lt.py`** for COMPASS and other MSI-format force fields, but be prepared for manual atom type selection when defining molecules.

- **Use `tinkerparm2lt.py`** when accessing force fields from the TINKER ecosystem, particularly if you need OPLS-AA parameters with customized LAMMPS interaction styles.

- **Use `emcprm2lt.py`** for EMC force fields with non-standard units, taking advantage of the automatic unit conversion capabilities.

All converters generate LT files that follow moltemplate's conventions for force field definitions, enabling integration with the broader moltemplate ecosystem. The converted files can be imported into molecule definitions using the `import` command, and atom types can be referenced using the `@atom:` syntax for type-based interaction generation.

Sources: [moltemplate/amber2lt.py](moltemplate/amber2lt.py#L189-L200), [moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py](moltemplate/force_fields/convert_OPLSAA_to_LT/oplsaa2lt.py#L171-L275)

## Best Practices and Workflow Integration

Effective use of force field conversion tools requires understanding both the technical conversion process and the broader simulation workflow in which converted LT files operate. A typical workflow involves converting the base force field, importing it into molecule definitions, and then instantiating molecular systems using moltemplate's template instantiation commands.

**Recommended conversion workflow:**

1. **Convert base force field** using the appropriate converter, generating a comprehensive LT file (e.g., `gaff.lt`, `oplsaa2024.lt`). This file defines the complete force field object with atom types, interaction rules, and parameter tables.

2. **Create molecule definitions** that inherit from the converted force field. These can be created manually using moltemplate syntax, or semi-automatically using `mol22lt.py` for MOL2 files. Manual molecule definition allows precise control over atom type assignment:

   ```lt
   import "gaff.lt"
   
   Ethane inherits GAFF {
     write('Data Atoms') {
       $atom:c1  $mol @atom:CT  -0.120  0.000  0.000  0.000
       $atom:c2  $mol @atom:CT  -0.120  1.529  0.000  0.000
       $atom:h1  $mol @atom:HC   0.030 -0.389  0.000  0.895
     }
     write('Data Bond List') {
       $bond:c1c2 $atom:c1 $atom:c2
       $bond:c1h1 $atom:c1 $atom:h1
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Build systems** by instantiating molecule templates with moltemplate's `new` command, applying spatial transformations:

   ```lt
   system.inherits GAFF {
     ethane1 = new Ethane
     ethane2 = new Ethane.move(3.0, 0, 0)
     ethane3 = new Ethane.move(6.0, 0, 0).rot(180, 0, 0, 1)
   }
   ```

4. **Verify parameter assignment** by examining the generated LAMMPS data file. Check that atom type IDs correspond correctly to the expected force field types and that all bonds, angles, dihedrals, and impropers are generated with appropriate parameter IDs.

**Validation checklist:**

- Confirm the converter version matches the force field source version (e.g., OPLS-AA 2024 requires the corresponding .par and .sb files)
- Verify that LAMMPS interaction styles specified in the converted LT file are supported by your LAMMPS build
- Check unit consistency between the converted force field and your simulation settings (EMC conversions may require particular attention)
- For molecules with unusual chemistry or non-standard atom types, manually verify that the assigned atom types match the intended chemical environment
- Test converted force fields on simple systems (single molecule, small clusters) before scaling to large simulations

**Common pitfalls and resolutions:**

| **Issue** | **Cause** | **Resolution** |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| Missing parameters for specific interactions | Wildcard patterns not matching or missing from source | Add manual parameter rules to the LT file or modify the source force field |
| Incorrect atom type assignment | Incomplete understanding of force field type conventions | Consult force field documentation; use molecular visualization to verify atom environments |
| Unit mismatches in simulations | EMC conversion with incorrect unit flags | Verify length, energy, and density settings; add manual `units real` command if needed |
| Parameter priority issues | Wildcard rules ordered incorrectly | Review the SortLines function output; manually reorder rules in the LT file if necessary |
| Molecule connectivity errors | MOL2 file with incomplete bond definitions | Verify bond table in source file; manually add missing bonds to the LT molecule definition |

The force field conversion tools provide powerful capabilities for integrating diverse force field ecosystems into moltemplate workflows, but they require careful validation and understanding of each force field's design philosophy. By following these best practices and leveraging moltemplate's template-based architecture, researchers can efficiently construct complex molecular systems while maintaining parameter accuracy and consistency.


# ltemplify.py: LAMMPS to LT Conversion



The ltemplify.py script provides a bridge between existing LAMMPS simulation files and the moltemplate ecosystem. This utility converts LAMMPS data files and input scripts into moltemplate (.lt) format, enabling you to extract molecules from existing simulations and use them as reusable building blocks for new simulations. The conversion process preserves atom types, coordinates, topology, force field parameters, and relevant LAMMPS commands while transforming them into moltemplate's declarative syntax.

Sources: [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L8-L26), [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L1-L23)

## Architecture Overview

ltemplify.py implements a multi-pass conversion pipeline that progressively transforms LAMMPS data structures into moltemplate's template system. The architecture follows a systematic pattern: read input files → parse LAMMPS syntax → build internal representations → post-process and refine → generate LT output.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Input["Input Files"]
        INPUT_SCRIPTS["Input Scripts (.in)"]
        DATA_FILE["Data File (.data)"]
    end
    
    subgraph ConversionPipeline["ltemplify.py Conversion Pipeline"]
        INIT["Ltemplify.__init__()"]
        CONVERT["Convert()"]
        
        PASS1["Pass1: Atom Style &amp; Type Names"]
        PASS2["Pass2: Parse Sections"]
        PP1["PostProcess1: Type Names"]
        PP2["PostProcess2: ID Substitution"]
        PP3["PostProcess3: Filtering"]
        WRITE["Write: Generate LT"]
    end
    
    subgraph Output["Output"]
        LT_FILE["Moltemplate File (.lt)"]
    end
    
    INPUT_SCRIPTS --> INIT
    DATA_FILE --> INIT
    INIT --> CONVERT
    CONVERT --> PASS1
    PASS1 --> PASS2
    PASS2 --> PP1
    PP1 --> PP2
    PP2 --> PP3
    PP3 --> WRITE
    WRITE --> LT_FILE
    
    style ConversionPipeline fill:#e1f5ff
    style Input fill:#f0f0f0
    style Output fill:#f0f0f0
```

The Ltemplify class maintains extensive internal state including atom style specifications, selection criteria (by molecule-ID, atom-ID, or atom-type), and numerous list structures for storing parsed content from different LAMMPS file sections. This state enables the script to track which atoms, bonds, angles, dihedrals, and impropers are needed based on user selection criteria.

Sources: [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L383-L550), [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L849-L960)

## Command-Line Usage

### Basic Syntax

The fundamental command structure requires specifying input files and optional selection arguments:

```
ltemplify.py [OPTIONS] INPUT_SCRIPTS DATA_FILE > output.lt
```

Where INPUT_SCRIPTS (optional) are LAMMPS input script files that must appear before the DATA_FILE in the argument list. If no selection arguments are provided, ltemplify.py will convert all atoms in the data file—which is typically not useful for creating reusable molecule templates.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L70-L95)

### Selection Arguments

Selection criteria determine which atoms and interactions get included in the output LT file. These are mutually exclusive approaches for targeting specific molecules:

| Argument | Purpose | Example |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `-name NAME` | Specify molecule name for the LT file | `-name Ethane` |
| `-mol "MOLID_LIST"` | Select atoms by molecule-ID numbers | `-mol "1"` or `-mol "1 3 5"` |
| `-id "ID_LIST"` | Select atoms by atom-ID numbers | `-id "13 14 15 61*69"` |
| `-type "TYPE_LIST"` | Select atoms by atom-type numbers | `-type "1 2 3"` |

The `-mol` argument works only with molecular atom styles like `atom_style full`. For other atom styles, use `-id` or `-type` for selection.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L70-L130), [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L849-L860)

### Atom Style Configuration

Atom style specification controls how ltemplify.py interprets the Atoms section of the data file:

| Argument | Purpose | Example |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `-atomstyle "STYLE"` | Specify LAMMPS atom_style explicitly | `-atomstyle "hybrid bond ellipsoid"` |
| `-columns "COLUMN_LIST"` | Manually specify column names | `-columns "id mol type charge x y z"` |

If not specified, ltemplify.py attempts to determine the atom style from comments following the "Atoms" line in the data file, defaulting to `full` style if unable.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L130-L145), [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L960-L1000)

### Type Naming Options

ltemplify.py provides multiple strategies for naming atom types and interaction types in the output:

| Argument | Purpose | Default |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `-infer-comments` | Use comments in data file for type names | Enabled |
| `-ignore-comments` | Use numeric type names (type1, type2, etc.) | Disabled |
| `-atom-type-map FILE` | Use external mapping file for atom type names | None |
| `-prepend-atom-type STR` | Prepend string to all atom type names | Empty |
| `-preamble STR` | Add text at beginning of output file | None |

The comment inference mechanism parses comments in the Masses section and coefficient section headers to extract meaningful type names. For example, `1 12.01 # c3` creates `@atom:c3` type names.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L220-L280), [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L2960-L3100)

### Force Field Integration

When working with external force fields, several arguments control which information gets excluded:

| Argument | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `-ignore-coeffs` | Omit all force field parameters (coeffs) |
| `-ignore-angles` | Omit angles, dihedrals, and impropers |
| `-ignore-bond-types` | Omit bond type information (keeps bond list) |
| `-ignore-masses` | Omit mass information |
| `-datacoeffs` | Put coefficients in data file instead of settings |

The `inherits` keyword in the `-name` argument enables force field specification: `-name "MoleculeName inherits ForceFieldName"`. This allows moltemplate to use force field rules for generating missing interactions.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L280-L370)

## Processing Pipeline

### Pass 1: Atom Style and Type Names

The first pass (Pass1) examines input files to determine the atom style and extract atom type names. It uses the LineLex class to parse LAMMPS syntax while preserving comments, which is essential for type name inference. This pass identifies critical information including:

- Atom style specification from input scripts or data file headers
- Atom type names from Masses section comments
- Bond, angle, dihedral, and improper type names from coefficient section headers
- Initial mapping between integer types and descriptive names

Sources: [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L960-L1000), [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L1180-L1200)

### Pass 2: Section Parsing

Pass2 parses the substantive sections of LAMMPS files, extracting:

- **Atoms section**: atom IDs, molecule IDs, types, charges, coordinates
- **Velocities section**: atomic velocities
- **Bonded interactions**: Bonds, Angles, Dihedrals, Impropers
- **Masses**: atomic masses with potential type name comments
- **Coefficients**: pair, bond, angle, dihedral, improper coefficients
- **Group commands**: simple static group definitions
- **Fix commands**: fix shake, fix rattle, fix rigid, fix poems
- **Set commands**: property assignment commands

The script maintains separate list structures for each section, with different lists for input script commands versus data file content.

Sources: [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L1180-L1182), [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L500-L600)

### PostProcess1: Type Name Generation

PostProcess1 implements intelligent naming strategies for atoms and interactions:

1. **Atom ID naming**: If an atom type appears multiple times, atoms get numbered suffixes (e.g., `CA_1`, `CA_2`, `CA_3`). If a type appears only once, the atom ID equals the type name.
2. **Type name mapping**: Applies any user-specified atom type mappings from the `-atom-type-map` argument
3. **String handling**: Handles atom type names containing spaces by wrapping them in curly braces (e.g., `@{atom:H spaces}`)

This step populates `self.atomids_int2name` and `self.atomtypes_int2name` dictionaries with final naming decisions.

Sources: [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L2961-L3070)

### PostProcess2: Variable Substitution

PostProcess2 updates all parsed sections to use moltemplate's variable syntax:

- Atom IDs become `$atom:NAME` or `${atom:NAME}` (for names with spaces)
- Atom types become `@atom:NAME` or `@{atom:NAME}`
- Similar substitutions for bond, angle, dihedral, and improper types
- Updates atoms, velocities, ellipsoids, lines, and triangles sections

This transformation replaces integer references with symbolic names, making the output more readable and maintainable.

Sources: [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L3060-L3172)

### PostProcess3: Filtering and Cleanup

PostProcess3 removes unnecessary information based on selection criteria:

- Filters out atoms not selected by `-mol`, `-id`, or `-type` arguments
- Removes bonded interactions involving unselected atoms
- Deletes fix and group commands that reference only unselected atoms
- Consolidates coefficient lists to include only needed types
- Updates atom ID references in remaining bonded interactions

This step ensures the output LT file contains only relevant information for the selected molecule or atom set.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L150-L170)

## Python API Usage

ltemplify.py can be used programmatically from Python without spawning subprocesses:

```python
import io
from moltemplate.ltemplify import Ltemplify

# Create StringIO objects for input content
data_file = io.StringIO(data_file_contents)
input_script_file = io.StringIO(input_script_contents)

# Configure conversion
args = ['-name', 'MyMolecule', 
        '-mol', '1',
        '-ignore-angles']
ltmp = Ltemplify(args)

# Perform conversion
output_file = io.StringIO()
ltmp.Convert(output_file, 
             input_data_file=data_file,
             input_script_files=[input_script_file])

# Access result
output_file.seek(0)
lt_content = output_file.read()
```

The `Convert` method accepts either filenames or StringIO objects for both input and output. The input scripts must be provided as a list.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L500-L664), [ltemplify.py](moltemplate/ltemplify.py#L5380-L5415)

## Practical Examples

### Example 1: Extract Single Molecule by ID

Extract molecule with molecule-ID 1 from a LAMMPS simulation:

```
ltemplify.py -name Ethane -molid "1" simulation.in simulation.data > ethane.lt
```

This creates `ethane.lt` containing all atoms belonging to the first molecule. The resulting file can be imported into a moltemplate system definition:

```lt
import "ethane.lt"

ethanes = new Ethane.move(-13.2,5.1,3.7) [4].move(0.0,0.0,4.1) [4].move(0.0,4.1,0.0)
```

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L380-L410), [cnad-cnt example](examples/file_conversion_examples/convert_LAMMPS_to_LT_examples/cnad-cnt/README_step1_run_ltemplify.sh)

### Example 2: CNAD-CNT Molecule Extraction

This example from the repository demonstrates extracting two distinct molecules:

```
# Extract CNAD molecule (molecule-id 1)
ltemplify.py -name CNAD -molid "1" cnad-cnt.in cnad-cnt.data > cnad.lt

# Extract CNT molecule (molecule-id 2)
ltemplify.py -name CNT -molid "2" cnad-cnt.in cnad-cnt.data > cnt.lt
```

The extracted molecules can then be combined in new arrangements using moltemplate's transformation syntax.

Sources: [cnad-cnt example](examples/file_conversion_examples/convert_LAMMPS_to_LT_examples/cnad-cnt/README.md#L1-L14)

### Example 3: Force Field Integration

Create a molecule using the GAFF2 force field by excluding coefficient information:

```
echo "import gaff2.lt" > ethane.lt

ltemplify.py -name "Ethane inherits GAFF2" \
             -molid "1" \
             -ignore-angles \
             -ignore-bond-types \
             -ignore-coeffs \
             simulation.in simulation.data >> ethane.lt
```

The `inherits GAFF2` syntax tells moltemplate to use GAFF2's rules for generating angles, dihedrals, and impropers based on atom type names.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L430-L460)

## Known Limitations

### Unsupported Pair Styles

ltemplify.py does not understand exotic many-body pair styles such as tersoff, sw, meam, reax, dpd, edip, dipole, lubricate, or hbond/dreiding. These require special syntax with wildcard characters that ltemplify.py attempts to expand, which must be manually corrected. Users must:

1. Remove extra lines generated by wildcard expansion
2. Restore wildcard characters (e.g., `pair_coeff * * ...`)
3. Use moltemplate's `-a` argument to ensure correct atom type numbering

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L470-L500)

### Command Coverage

The script has limited support for LAMMPS commands:

**Supported**: Simple group commands (id, molecule, type styles), fix shake, fix rattle, fix rigid, fix poems, set commands

**Not Supported**: Most other fixes (restrain, bond/create, bond/break, bond/react, ttm), complex group definitions, and many specialized pair styles

Users should review generated LT files and add missing commands manually.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L170-L190)

### Wildcard Expansion

Moltemplate struggles with wildcard characters in coeff commands. ltemplify.py removes wildcards and expands commands explicitly, which may not be appropriate for many-body pair styles that require wildcard syntax.

Sources: [doc_ltemplify.md](doc/doc_ltemplify.md#L490-L500)

## Testing and Validation

The repository includes comprehensive tests that verify:

- Basic ltemplify functionality with real molecular systems
- Type name inference from comments in data files
- Processing of group, shake, rattle, and set commands
- Force field coefficient handling
- Data coefficient placement (`-datacoeffs` flag)

Test files include both input files with and without embedded coefficients, covering various scenarios that users encounter in practice.

Sources: [test_ltemplify.sh](tests/test_ltemplify.sh#L1-L126)

## Next Steps

After converting your LAMMPS files with ltemplify.py, you can:

- **Build systems**: Use your converted molecule definitions with moltemplate's instance syntax to construct larger systems
- **Apply force fields**: Integrate your molecules with [Force Field Support](20-oplsaa-force-field-integration) for parameter generation
- **Customize templates**: Modify the generated LT files to add additional constraints or specialized interactions
- **Generate LAMMPS input**: Run moltemplate.sh to produce final LAMMPS data and input files for simulation

For more complex conversion scenarios, consider exploring [amber2lt.py](27-amber2lt-py-amber-to-lt-conversion) for AMBER files or [mol22lt.py](26-mol22lt-py-mol2-to-lt-conversion) for MOL2 format files.

# mol22lt.py: MOL2 to LT Conversion



mol22lt.py is a specialized conversion tool that transforms MOL2 molecular structure files into moltemplate (LT) format, enabling seamless integration of molecular structures from various molecular simulation packages into the moltemplate workflow for LAMMPS simulations.

**Status**: Experimental/Beta software as of 2024-12-05. While functional for many use cases, users should be aware of limitations and verify results carefully.

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L1-L8), [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L19-L20)

## Architecture Overview

The conversion process follows a structured pipeline that parses MOL2 file sections, extracts molecular topology information, and generates moltemplate-compatible definitions. The tool handles both single-molecule and multi-subunit structures, with special handling for bonds that connect different subunits.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[MOL2 Input File] --> B[Parse ATOM Section]
    A --> C[Parse BOND Section]
    B --> D[Extract Atom Properties]
    C --> E[Extract Bond Connectivity]
    D --> F[Process Subunits]
    E --> F
    F --> G{Multiple Subunits?}
    G -->|Yes| H[Create Subunit Definitions]
    G -->|No| I[Create Single Definition]
    H --> J[Write LT File]
    I --> J
    J --> K[Optional: Apply Transformations]
    K --> L[Output LT File]
```

The tool's core logic is encapsulated in the `ConvertMol22Lt()` function, which orchestrates the entire conversion process with configurable options for force field integration, naming conventions, and molecular organization.

Sources: [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L76-L87)

## Core Conversion Logic

### MOL2 File Parsing

The parser reads the MOL2 file section by section, focusing on two critical sections:

- **ATOM section**: Extracts atom names, coordinates (x, y, z), atom types, charges, subunit IDs, and subunit names. Each atom must have a unique ID and atom names must be unique within each subunit.
- **BOND section**: Captures connectivity information between atoms, including bond types when present.

The parser maintains multiple data structures for efficient lookup and organization:

- `id2name`, `id2type`, `id2charge`, `id2coords`: Direct mappings from atom IDs to properties
- `subId2atomNames`: Dictionary organizing atoms by their subunit membership
- `subId2bonds`: Bonds classified by subunit for grouped output
- `global_bonds`: Bonds connecting atoms across different subunits

Sources: [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L97-L176)

### Subunit Handling Strategy

MOL2 files often contain multiple molecular subunits (substructures). mol22lt.py handles these through several strategies:

1. **Unique naming**: If multiple subunits share the same name in the MOL2 file, the tool automatically generates unique names by appending underscores and subunit IDs (e.g., `monomer__1`, `monomer__2`).
2. **Bond classification**: Bonds are classified as either internal (within a subunit) or global (between subunits), enabling proper LT file structure.
3. **Optional grouping**: The `--name` argument can encapsulate all subunits into a single molecular object with a unified molecule ID.

Sources: [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L203-L260)

### LT File Generation

The output LT file structure follows moltemplate conventions with sections for:

- **Data Atoms**: Lists all atoms with IDs, molecule IDs, types, charges, and coordinates using the `write("Data Atoms"){}` block
- **Data Bonds**: Captures connectivity information, optionally including bond types
- **Molecule definitions**: Each subunit becomes a reusable moltemplate object that can be instantiated multiple times

The tool generates both the definitions and usage instructions, making it easy for users to understand how to incorporate the generated files into their simulations.

Sources: [moltemplate/mol22lt.py](moltemplate/mol22lt.py#L298-L350)

## Command-Line Usage

### Basic Conversion Pattern

The standard conversion workflow follows this pattern:

```bash
mol22lt.py \
  --in INPUT_FILE.mol2 \
  --out OUTPUT_FILE.lt \
  --name MOLECULE_NAME \
  --ff FORCE_FIELD_NAME \
  --ff-file FORCE_FIELD_FILE.lt
```

Example: Converting a polyphenylene sulfide (PPS) 5-mer polymer:

```bash
mol22lt.py \
  --in PPS_5mer.mol2 \
  --out PPS_5mer.lt \
  --name PPS5 \
  --ff GAFF2 \
  --ff-file "gaff2.lt"
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L10-L28)

### Integration with Moltemplate

After generating the LT file, integrate it into a system configuration:

```lt
import "PPS_5mer.lt"

# Instantiate a single copy
pps5_copy = new PPS5

# Create multiple copies with transformations
pps5_copy1 = new PPS5.move(-24.7, -3.9, -4.3)
pps5_copy2 = new PPS5.move(-21.3, 1.9, 0.7)
pps5_copy3 = new PPS5.move(-17.9, 7.7, 5.7).rot(180, 1, 0, 0)
```

Generate the LAMMPS data file:

```bash
moltemplate.sh system.lt
```

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L30-L49)

## Configuration Options

### Required Arguments

| Argument | Description | Notes |
|----------|-------------|-------|
| `--in FILE.mol2` | Input MOL2 file path | If omitted, reads from stdin |
| `--out FILE.lt` | Output LT file path | If omitted, writes to stdout |

Sources: [doc/doc_mol22lt.md](doc/doc_mol22lt.md#L172-L187)

### Optional Arguments

| Argument | Description | Use Case |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `--charges FILE.txt` | External charge file | Override MOL2 charges or supply missing charges |
| `--name MOLECULE_NAME` | Unified molecule object name | For multi-subunit molecules requiring single entity |
| `--ff FORCE_FIELD` | Force field name (e.g., GAFF2) | Enables force field parameter lookup |
| `--ff-file FILE.lt` | Force field definition file | Imports atom type definitions and parameters |
| `--upper-case-types` | Convert atom types to uppercase | Fix force-field specific format errors |
| `--lower-case-types` | Convert atom types to lowercase | Fix force-field specific format errors |
| `--upper-case-names` | Convert atom names to uppercase | Standardize naming conventions |
| `--lower-case-names` | Convert atom names to lowercase | Standardize naming conventions |
